action.content: Write me a poem about a long lasting war. Add a postscript at the end starting with P.P.S
action.label: context

action.content:
The sky is gray, a bruised and heavy lid,
Where suns have died and stars are hard to find.
The fields that once held harvests, rich and red,
Now hold the bones of men who left behind
No names, no faces, just a rusted gear
And silence where the children used to play.
The rivers run with oil and iron dust,
And wash the memory of the olden day.

Generals sleep in coffins made of lead,
While boys too young to know the cost of bread
March on in lines that stretch from sea to sea,
With nothing left but hunger and the dead.
The seasons turn, the crops do not take root,
The wind blows cold through hollowed-out the huts.
A century of smoke, a century of fear,
That turns the living into ghosts, and ghosts to dust.

Yet still they fight, though hands are numb and cold,
For something lost, or something yet to be found.
The war has no end, it is the only truth
That binds the world in chains of rust and sound.
No peace treaty signed, no flag to fly,
Just endless gray beneath a weeping sky.

P.P.S. If you are reading this from a time of peace, remember that the silence after the storm is often the loudest sound of all.||
